Hatsvali and Tetnuldi Ski Areas

Mestia's two ski zones — Hatsvali with sheltered forest runs, and Tetnuldi, where the lifts pass 3,000 metres.

Time needed
6 h
From Tbilisi
478 km · 8:50
Road
Mostly paved
Car needed
Crossover / SUV
Season
December–March
Entry
~30 ₾

Upper Svaneti has two ski areas, and they complement each other rather than compete. Hatsvali lies eight kilometres from Mestia, starts at about 1,870 metres and is defined by runs cut through forest: short, sheltered from wind and comfortable for intermediate skiers. Its gondola also operates in summer, and plenty of visitors ride it in July and August purely for the view.

Tetnuldi sits 15–16 kilometres from Mestia, higher and considerably more serious. Its lift system takes skiers above three thousand metres, opening onto wide treeless slopes. This is one of the highest lift-served points in Georgia, and the panorama across Shkhara, Ushba and Tetnuldi itself justifies the ticket on its own.

The practical differences:

  • Hatsvali — short access road, forest runs, less wind, modest vertical
  • Tetnuldi — longer and partly rough access, alpine terrain, much bigger descent
  • Both areas run a short season and have simpler infrastructure than Gudauri

Equipment rental exists at both bases, but the range is limited, so bring your own boots if you have them. Regular transfers run from Mestia centre to each area, which many people prefer to driving. Neither resort has the queues or the nightlife of larger Georgian resorts, and that is a large part of the appeal here.

Practical advice

The season runs roughly from late December to late March, though snow quality varies sharply from year to year, so check conditions before committing. Both bases have a small cafe but no ATM: carry cash in lari. Tetnuldi is colder and windier, so a face mask and warm gloves are genuinely needed. Parking at each base is free and rarely full. Winter tyres are compulsory in the season and chains are worth having in the car, particularly for the upper part of the Tetnuldi road.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Tbilisi to Mestia is 470 km and eight to nine hours via Zugdidi and the Enguri gorge. From Mestia, Hatsvali is eight kilometres of paved switchbacks, about twenty minutes. Tetnuldi is 15–16 km and takes over half an hour: part of the road is asphalt, part is gravel and gets churned up in winter. That is why a high-clearance car on winter tyres is the sensible choice here. Fill up in Mestia, since there is no fuel at either base. In poor weather an organised transfer from town is the easier option.

Nearby places

Town

Mestia and the Svan Towers

Upper Svaneti's main town at 1,500 m — medieval stone defence towers, two strong museums and the trailhead for every route in the region.

Lake

Koruldi Lakes

Small alpine pools at 2,740 m above Mestia, facing Mount Ushba — reachable only by 4x4 or on foot.

Mountain

Chalaadi Glacier

The most accessible glacier near Mestia — a short drive up the valley and a two-hour walk to the ice tongue.
